Solver returned keys 'set_1','set_2' — mismatch. So the failure is key naming contract: task says "keys are identifiers for each set" but doesn't specify dict input; solver chose to iterate list-like. Actually solver's code: if entry is dict, take fields; else unpack. If data were a dict, iterating gives keys (strings), which would fail unpacking... but the failure is set(report) != set(expected_output) — keys differ. Also solver catches exceptions and returns error strings instead of raising — but test would fail at the key assertion first.

So the primary failure: EVAL_CONTRACT / TASK_EXECUTION — misread input schema (dict keyed by identifiers, not list).
